claim: Antigen Ki-67 is a nuclear protein expressed in proliferating mammalian cells.
source: Antigen Ki-67 is a nuclear protein expressed in proliferating mammalian cells.
evidence: This is a foundational statement in the abstract supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: Ki-67 is widely used in cancer histopathology.
source: It is widely used in cancer histopathology but its functions remain unclear.
evidence: This reflects established clinical practice in cancer diagnosis.

claim: The functions of Ki-67 remain unclear.
source: It is widely used in cancer histopathology but its functions remain unclear.
evidence: This statement sets up the research question and is supported by the need for this study.

claim: Altering Ki-67 expression levels did not significantly affect cell proliferation in vivo.
source: Altering Ki-67 expression levels did not significantly affect cell proliferation in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental work presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ki-67 mutant mice developed normally.
source: Ki-67 mutant mice developed normally and cells lacking Ki-67 proliferated efficiently.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the TALEN-mediated Ki-67 mutant mice described in the manuscript.

claim: Cells lacking Ki-67 proliferated efficiently.
source: Ki-67 mutant mice developed normally and cells lacking Ki-67 proliferated efficiently.
evidence: This is demonstrated through multiple cell line experiments and mouse models presented in the manuscript.

claim: Upregulation of Ki-67 expression in differentiated tissues did not prevent cell cycle arrest.
source: Conversely, upregulation of Ki-67 expression in differentiated tissues did not prevent cell cycle arrest.
evidence: This is supported by experiments with Fzr1 knockout mice shown in Figure 2.

claim: Ki-67 interactors included proteins involved in nucleolar processes and chromatin regulators.
source: Ki-67 interactors included proteins involved in nucleolar processes and chromatin regulators.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry analysis of Ki-67 immunoprecipitates shown in Figure 6.

claim: Ki-67 depletion disrupted nucleologenesis.
source: Ki-67 depletion disrupted nucleologenesis but did not inhibit pre-rRNA processing.
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence experiments showing disrupted perichromosomal region formation in Figure 7B.

claim: Ki-67 depletion did not inhibit pre-rRNA processing.
source: Ki-67 depletion disrupted nucleologenesis but did not inhibit pre-rRNA processing.
evidence: This is supported by Northern blot analysis of pre-rRNA intermediates shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Ki-67 depletion altered gene expression.
source: In contrast, it altered gene expression.
evidence: This is demonstrated by genome-wide transcriptome analysis shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Ki-67 silencing disrupted heterochromatin compaction.
source: Ki-67 silencing also had wide-ranging effects on chromatin organisation, disrupting heterochromatin compaction and long-range genomic interactions.
evidence: This is supported by FRET-FLIM analysis shown in Figure 9B-D.

claim: Ki-67 silencing disrupted long-range genomic interactions.
source: Ki-67 silencing also had wide-ranging effects on chromatin organisation, disrupting heterochromatin compaction and long-range genomic interactions.
evidence: This is demonstrated by CENP-A localization studies shown in Figure 9E.

claim: Trimethylation of histone H3K9 and H4K20 was relocalised within the nucleus upon Ki-67 depletion.
source: Trimethylation of histone H3K9 and H4K20 was relocalised within the nucleus.
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence analysis in Figures 10 and Figure 10—figure supplements 1-3.

claim: Overexpression of human Ki-67 induced ectopic heterochromatin formation.
source: Finally, overexpression of human or Xenopus Ki-67 induced ectopic heterochromatin formation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence showing DAPI-dense foci and H3K9me3 enrichment in Figure 11A.

claim: Overexpression of Xenopus Ki-67 induced ectopic heterochromatin formation.
source: Finally, overexpression of human or Xenopus Ki-67 induced ectopic heterochromatin formation.
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence analysis in Figure 11C.

claim: Ki-67 expression in proliferating cells spatially organises heterochromatin, thereby controlling gene expression.
source: Altogether, our results suggest that Ki-67 expression in proliferating cells spatially organises heterochromatin, thereby controlling gene expression.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the collective experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ki-67 is constitutively expressed in cycling mammalian cells.
source: The cell proliferation antigen Ki-67 (Ki-67 or Ki67) is constitutively expressed in cycling mammalian cells (Gerdes et al., 1983).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 is a nuclear DNA-binding protein.
source: Ki-67 is a nuclear DNA-binding protein (MacCallum and Hall, 2000) with two human isoforms that have predicted molecular weights of 320kDa and 359kDa (Gerdes et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 has two human isoforms with predicted molecular weights of 320kDa and 359kDa.
source: Ki-67 is a nuclear DNA-binding protein (MacCallum and Hall, 2000) with two human isoforms that have predicted molecular weights of 320kDa and 359kDa (Gerdes et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: All Ki-67 homologues contain an N-terminal Forkhead-associated (FHA) domain.
source: All homologues contain an N-terminal Forkhead-associated (FHA) domain, which can bind both to DNA and to phosphorylated epitopes.
evidence: This is a structural characterization based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The FHA domain of Ki-67 can bind both to DNA and to phosphorylated epitopes.
source: All homologues contain an N-terminal Forkhead-associated (FHA) domain, which can bind both to DNA and to phosphorylated epitopes.
evidence: This is based on known properties of FHA domains.

claim: The most characteristic feature of Ki-67 is the presence of multiple tandem repeats containing a conserved motif of unknown function, the 'Ki-67 domain'.
source: The most characteristic feature of Ki-67 is the presence of multiple tandem repeats (14 in mice, 16 in human) containing a conserved motif of unknown function, the 'Ki-67 domain'.
evidence: This is shown in the domain structure diagram in Figure 1A.

claim: Mouse Ki-67 contains 14 tandem repeats.
source: The most characteristic feature of Ki-67 is the presence of multiple tandem repeats (14 in mice, 16 in human) containing a conserved motif of unknown function, the 'Ki-67 domain'.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Human Ki-67 contains 16 tandem repeats.
source: The most characteristic feature of Ki-67 is the presence of multiple tandem repeats (14 in mice, 16 in human) containing a conserved motif of unknown function, the 'Ki-67 domain'.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Ki-67 contains a Protein Phosphatase 1 (PP1)-binding motif.
source: Two other conserved motifs include a Protein Phosphatase 1 (PP1)-binding motif (Booth et al., 2014) and a 31 amino acid conserved domain (CD) of unknown function, 100% identical between human and mouse, that includes a 22 amino acid motif conserved in all homologues.
evidence: This is supported by a citation and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Ki-67 contains a 31 amino acid conserved domain (CD) of unknown function that is 100% identical between human and mouse.
source: Two other conserved motifs include a Protein Phosphatase 1 (PP1)-binding motif (Booth et al., 2014) and a 31 amino acid conserved domain (CD) of unknown function, 100% identical between human and mouse, that includes a 22 amino acid motif conserved in all homologues.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The conserved domain of Ki-67 includes a 22 amino acid motif conserved in all homologues.
source: Two other conserved motifs include a Protein Phosphatase 1 (PP1)-binding motif (Booth et al., 2014) and a 31 amino acid conserved domain (CD) of unknown function, 100% identical between human and mouse, that includes a 22 amino acid motif conserved in all homologues.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Ki-67 homologues have a weakly conserved leucine/arginine rich C-terminus which can bind to DNA.
source: Ki-67 homologues also have a weakly conserved leucine/arginine rich C-terminus which can bind to DNA and, when overexpressed, promotes chromatin compaction (Scholzen et al., 2002; Takagi et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: When overexpressed, the C-terminus of Ki-67 promotes chromatin compaction.
source: Ki-67 homologues also have a weakly conserved leucine/arginine rich C-terminus which can bind to DNA and, when overexpressed, promotes chromatin compaction (Scholzen et al., 2002; Takagi et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 protein levels vary through the cell cycle.
source: Ki-67 protein levels and localisation vary through the cell cycle.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Ki-67 localisation varies through the cell cycle.
source: Ki-67 protein levels and localisation vary through the cell cycle.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Maximum Ki-67 expression is found in G2 phase or during mitosis.
source: Its maximum expression is found in G2 phase or during mitosis (Endl and Gerdes, 2000b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: In interphase, Ki-67 forms fibre-like structures in fibrillarin-deficient regions surrounding nucleoli.
source: In interphase, Ki-67 forms fibre-like structures in fibrillarin-deficient regions surrounding nucleoli (Verheijen et al., 1989b; Kill, 1996; Cheutin et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 colocalises with satellite DNA.
source: Ki-67 also colocalises with satellite DNA (Bridger et al., 1998) and is found in protein complexes that bind to satellite DNA (Saksouk et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 is found in protein complexes that bind to satellite DNA.
source: Ki-67 also colocalises with satellite DNA (Bridger et al., 1998) and is found in protein complexes that bind to satellite DNA (Saksouk et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 remains associated with nucleolar organiser regions of acrocentric chromosomes throughout interphase.
source: It remains associated with nucleolar organiser regions of acrocentric chromosomes throughout interphase (Bridger et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 is a direct substrate of the cyclin-dependent kinase CDK1.
source: Ki-67 is a direct substrate of the cyclin-dependent kinase CDK1 (Blethrow et al., 2008) and is hyperphosphorylated in mitosis.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 is hyperphosphorylated in mitosis.
source: Ki-67 is a direct substrate of the cyclin-dependent kinase CDK1 (Blethrow et al., 2008) and is hyperphosphorylated in mitosis.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Hyperphosphorylation may regulate Ki-67 expression and/or localisation.
source: This may regulate its expression and / or localisation (Endl and Gerdes, 2000a).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by a citation.

claim: In HeLa cells, Ki-67 binds tightly to chromatin in interphase.
source: In HeLa cells, Ki-67 binds tightly to chromatin in interphase, whereas this binding is weakened in mitosis (Saiwaki et al., 2005) when it associates with condensed chromosomes before relocating to the chromosome periphery (Verheijen et al., 1989a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 binding to chromatin is weakened in mitosis.
source: In HeLa cells, Ki-67 binds tightly to chromatin in interphase, whereas this binding is weakened in mitosis (Saiwaki et al., 2005) when it associates with condensed chromosomes before relocating to the chromosome periphery (Verheijen et al., 1989a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: In mitosis, Ki-67 associates with condensed chromosomes before relocating to the chromosome periphery.
source: In HeLa cells, Ki-67 binds tightly to chromatin in interphase, whereas this binding is weakened in mitosis (Saiwaki et al., 2005) when it associates with condensed chromosomes before relocating to the chromosome periphery (Verheijen et al., 1989a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 is generally assumed to be required for cell proliferation.
source: Ki-67 is generally assumed to be required for cell proliferation.
evidence: This reflects the prevailing view in the field that the authors are challenging.

claim: Injection of antisense oligonucleotides that block Ki-67 expression inhibited cell proliferation in an early study.
source: An early study found that injection of antisense oligonucleotides that block Ki-67 expression inhibited cell proliferation (Schluter et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Unperturbed Ki-67 expression levels are required for normal proliferation rates in various cell lines according to subsequent studies.
source: Subsequent studies have shown that unperturbed Ki-67 expression levels are required for normal proliferation rates in various cell lines (Kausch et al., 2003; Rahmanzadeh et al., 2007; Zheng et al., 2006; 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: No complete Ki-67 loss of function studies have been reported prior to this work.
source: However, no complete Ki-67 loss of function studies have been reported.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the literature that justifies the current study.

claim: The dynamic localisation of Ki-67 has led to suggestions that it could coordinate nucleolar disassembly and reassembly at either side of mitosis.
source: The dynamic localisation of Ki-67 has led to suggestions that it could coordinate nucleolar disassembly and reassembly at either side of mitosis (Schmidt et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 is required to localise nucleolar granular components to mitotic chromosomes.
source: Indeed, Ki-67 is required to localise nucleolar granular components to mitotic chromosomes, thereby potentially playing a role in nucleolar segregation between daughter cells (Booth et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 has been reported to have roles in ribosome biogenesis.
source: It has also been reported that Ki-67 has roles in ribosome biogenesis (Rahmanzadeh et al., 2007), consistent with its nucleolar localisation and apparent role in cell proliferation.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Mouse Ki-67 contains two D-boxes.
source: Human Ki-67 isoforms contain two or three KEN boxes, whereas mouse Ki-67 contains two D-boxes (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Human Ki-67 isoforms contain two or three KEN boxes.
source: Human Ki-67 isoforms contain two or three KEN boxes, whereas mouse Ki-67 contains two D-boxes (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Mouse Ki-67 contains a sequence highly similar to the A-box at position 2680-2687.
source: Mouse Ki-67 contains an additional sequence, AQRKQPSR at 2680–2687, which is highly similar to the A-box, a third APC/C-Cdh1 recognition motif (Littlepage and Ruderman, 2002).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and comparison to known APC/C recognition motifs.

claim: In Fzr1 knockout MEFs, Ki-67 was upregulated and more homogeneously expressed compared to heterozygous MEFs.
source: Asynchronous Fzr1 heterozygous MEFs, that are at different stages of the cell cycle, had variable Ki-67 levels, whereas in the Fzr1 knockout MEFs Ki-67 was upregulated and more homogeneously expressed (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence analysis in Figure 2A.

claim: In Fzr1-knockout mice, Ki-67 was overexpressed and uncoupled from cells that incorporate BrdU in all tissues examined.
source: Here, Ki-67 was overexpressed and uncoupled from cells that incorporate BrdU in all tissues examined (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by immunohistochemistry in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ki-67 expression is regulated by APC/C-Cdh1 in mice.
source: Thus, Ki-67 expression is regulated by APC/C-Cdh1 in mice and its downregulation is not a prerequisite for cell cycle exit.
evidence: This is inferred from the Fzr1 knockout experiments.

claim: Ki-67 downregulation is not a prerequisite for cell cycle exit.
source: Thus, Ki-67 expression is regulated by APC/C-Cdh1 in mice and its downregulation is not a prerequisite for cell cycle exit.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the observation that cells can exit the cell cycle despite sustained Ki-67 expression in Fzr1 knockout mice.

claim: A TALEN pair targeting the unique ATG start codon of Mki67 is predicted to generate null alleles.
source: To disrupt the gene encoding Ki-67, Mki67, in the mouse germline, we used a TALEN pair targeting the unique ATG start codon. This is predicted to generate null alleles (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on the design strategy shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: After cytoplasmic injection of TALEN-encoding mRNAs into zygotes, 10 out of 54 mice had mutations disrupting the coding sequence.
source: After cytoplasmic injection of these TALEN-encoding mRNAs into zygotes, 10 out of 54 mice had mutations disrupting the coding sequence.
evidence: This is experimental data from the TALEN mutagenesis procedure.

claim: Four founder mutant mice gave germline transmission of the mutation.
source: We crossed founder mutant mice, and four gave germline transmission of the mutation.
evidence: This is experimental data from breeding experiments.

claim: Germline transmission resulted in six lines: two with mutations eliminating the initiation codon and four with deletions causing frameshifts immediately downstream of the ATG.
source: Due to mosaicism, this resulted in six lines: two lines with mutations eliminating the initiation codon and four lines with deletions which cause frameshifts immediately downstream of the ATG (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Homozygous mutants were obtained at the expected Mendelian frequency.
source: We crossed these mice and, unexpectedly, obtained homozygous mutants at the expected Mendelian frequency that were indistinguishable from heterozygous or wild-type (WT) littermates (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is experimental data from breeding experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Homozygous Ki-67 mutants were indistinguishable from heterozygous or wild-type littermates.
source: We crossed these mice and, unexpectedly, obtained homozygous mutants at the expected Mendelian frequency that were indistinguishable from heterozygous or wild-type (WT) littermates (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Both Ki-67 deletion mutant lines showed normal growth and were fertile.
source: Both deletion mutant lines showed normal growth and were fertile.
evidence: This is observational data from mouse husbandry.

claim: Sagittal sections from Mki672nt∆/2nt∆ mice did not reveal any obvious defects in tissue morphology.
source: Sagittal sections from Mki672nt∆/2nt∆ mice did not reveal any obvious defects in tissue morphology (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown by histological analysis in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: In WT animals, the proliferative crypt compartment of the intestinal epithelium was strongly stained for Ki-67 by immunohistochemistry.
source: In WT animals, the proliferative crypt compartment was strongly stained for Ki-67 by immunohistochemistry (IHC), while only minimal levels of Ki-67 were observed in the differentiated cells on the villus (Figure 3C, top), as expected.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In Ki-67 mutants, proliferating crypt cells showed only residual levels of Ki-67 staining by IHC.
source: In contrast, in the mutants, proliferating crypt cells showed only residual levels of Ki-67 staining by IHC (Figure 3C, bottom) or immunofluorescence (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Immunoblotting of intestinal epithelium preparations detected a weak band of similar size to WT Ki-67 in mutants.
source: Immunoblotting of intestinal epithelium preparations could detect a weak band of similar size to WT Ki-67 (Figure 3D; Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The Ki-67 signal was reduced by at least 90% in both mutants compared to WT tissue.
source: The signal was, however, reduced by at least 90% in both mutants compared to WT tissue.
evidence: This is quantification of Western blot data.

claim: Three different Ki-67 antibodies gave similar results in detecting reduced Ki-67 levels in mutants.
source: Three different Ki-67 antibodies gave similar results.
evidence: This is experimental validation using multiple antibodies.

claim: Ki-67 mRNA level was increased rather than reduced in the intestinal tissue of mutants.
source: qRT-PCR analysis showed that Ki-67 mRNA level was, unexpectedly, increased rather than reduced in the intestinal tissue (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: Analysis of Wnt signalling and differentiation of goblet and tuft cells showed no differences between WT and Mki6721nt∆/21nt∆ mice in the intestinal epithelium.
source: In the intestinal epithelium, analysis of Wnt signalling and differentiation of goblet and tuft cells showed no differences between WT and Mki6721nt∆/21nt∆ mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is shown by immunohistochemistry in Figure 3—figure supplement 6.

claim: High Ki-67 levels are not required for development or differentiation in vivo.
source: These results show that high Ki-67 levels and an intact Ki-67 gene are not required for development or differentiation in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mouse mutant data.

claim: An intact Ki-67 gene is not required for development or differentiation in vivo.
source: These results show that high Ki-67 levels and an intact Ki-67 gene are not required for development or differentiation in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mouse mutant data.

claim: Homozygous Mki672nt∆/2nt∆ MEFs had at least 90% lower Ki-67 levels.
source: Homozygous Mki672nt∆/2nt∆MEFs had at least 90% lower Ki-67 levels (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is shown by Western blot in Figure 3E.

claim: In homozygous Ki-67 mutant MEFs, the Ki-67 mRNA level was increased to a level comparable with that of proliferating NIH-3T3 cells.
source: Indeed, in the homozygous mutant, the Ki-67 mRNA level was increased to a level comparable with that of proliferating NIH-3T3 cells.
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 7.

claim: Mutant MEFs proliferated comparably to controls.
source: Mutant MEF proliferated comparably to controls, and flow cytometric assessment of EdU incorporation after a 1 hr EdU pulse showed similar numbers of replicating cells in Ki-67 WT and mutant cells (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry data in Figure 3F.

claim: Flow cytometric assessment showed similar numbers of replicating cells in Ki-67 WT and mutant MEFs after a 1 hr EdU pulse.
source: Mutant MEF proliferated comparably to controls, and flow cytometric assessment of EdU incorporation after a 1 hr EdU pulse showed similar numbers of replicating cells in Ki-67 WT and mutant cells (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Nine monoclonal Ki-67 mutant NIH-3T3 cell lines were obtained with very low Ki-67 expression.
source: We obtained nine mutants with very low Ki-67 expression.
evidence: This is experimental data from the TALEN mutagenesis in NIH-3T3 cells.

claim: Five NIH-3T3 clones had biallelic mutations around the ATG codon.
source: Cloning and sequencing showed that five had biallelic mutations around the ATG codon (Figure 3—figure supplement 8).
evidence: This is shown by sequencing data in Figure 3—figure supplement 8.

claim: Ki-67 was barely detectable by Western blot in all NIH-3T3 mutant clones analysed.
source: As in mice, even though Ki-67 was visible by immunofluorescence, Ki-67 was barely detectable by Western blot in all clones analysed (Figure 3—figure supplement 9A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 9A.

claim: All NIH-3T3 Ki-67 mutant clones proliferated efficiently.
source: All clones proliferated efficiently (Figure 3—figure supplement 9B).
evidence: This is shown by growth curves in Figure 3—figure supplement 9B.

claim: In NIH-3T3 clones 14 and 21, there was no decrease in ribosome association with Ki-67 mRNA.
source: qRT-PCR quantification of Ki-67 mRNA from ribosome purifications shows that in clones 14 and 21 there was no decrease in ribosome association with Ki-67 mRNA; indeed, in clone 14 it increased, probably due to the higher Ki-67 mRNA level (Figure 3—figure supplement 10).
evidence: This is shown by polysome profiling data in Figure 3—figure supplement 10.

claim: In NIH-3T3 clone 14, ribosome association with Ki-67 mRNA increased, probably due to the higher Ki-67 mRNA level.
source: qRT-PCR quantification of Ki-67 mRNA from ribosome purifications shows that in clones 14 and 21 there was no decrease in ribosome association with Ki-67 mRNA; indeed, in clone 14 it increased, probably due to the higher Ki-67 mRNA level (Figure 3—figure supplement 10).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 10 and is an inference from the data.

claim: Ki-67 could not be positively identified in NIH-3T3 clones 14 and 21 by SILAC quantitative mass spectrometry.
source: Ki-67 could not be positively identified in clones 14 and 21 (Figure 3—figure supplement 11).
evidence: This is shown by mass spectrometry data in Figure 3—figure supplement 11.

claim: In peptides from WT NIH-3T3 cells, 44 peptides derived from Ki-67 were identified by MS/MS.
source: In peptides from WT cells (L), 44 peptides derived from Ki-67 were identified by MS/MS.
evidence: This is mass spectrometry data.

claim: In peptides from NIH-3T3 mutant cell lines, no MS/MS spectra for Ki-67 could be identified in either band.
source: In contrast, in peptides from mutant cell lines (H), no MS/MS spectra for Ki-67 could be identified in either band.
evidence: This is mass spectrometry data.

claim: In NIH-3T3 clone 14 band 1, the median normalised H/L intensity ratio of putative Ki-67 peaks was 0.095.
source: In band 1, the median normalised H/L intensity ratio of the 5 corresponding m/z peaks in clone 14 was 0.095 (mean, 0.100, SD, 0.02), and in clone 21 (7 peptides) was 0.191 (mean 0.203, SD 0.05).
evidence: This is quantitative mass spectrometry data.

claim: In NIH-3T3 clone 21 band 1, the median normalised H/L intensity ratio of putative Ki-67 peaks was 0.191.
source: In band 1, the median normalised H/L intensity ratio of the 5 corresponding m/z peaks in clone 14 was 0.095 (mean, 0.100, SD, 0.02), and in clone 21 (7 peptides) was 0.191 (mean 0.203, SD 0.05).
evidence: This is quantitative mass spectrometry data.

claim: If Ki67 is translated in the NIH-3T3 mutant cell lines, it is at trace levels that are not positively identifiable by state-of-the-art mass spectrometry.
source: Taken together, these results show that if Ki67 is translated in the mutant cell lines, it is at trace levels that are not positively identifiable by state-of-the-art mass spectrometry.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mass spectrometry data.

claim: At best, translation of Ki-67 can occur from the mutated Ki-67 gene with an estimated 10% efficiency.
source: At best, translation can occur from the mutated Ki-67 gene with an estimated 10% efficiency.
evidence: This is an estimate based on the mass spectrometry quantification.

claim: The residual Ki-67 product in mutants is most likely an N-terminally truncated protein lacking the conserved FHA-domain, arising from a downstream in-frame ATG.
source: The product is most likely an N-terminally truncated protein lacking the conserved FHA-domain, arising from a downstream in-frame ATG.
evidence: This is an inference based on the genetic mutations and translation initiation mechanisms.

claim: Several monoclonal cell lines were isolated in which Ki-67 mRNA was essentially eliminated using a double TALEN strategy.
source: We thus isolated several monoclonal cell lines in which Ki-67 mRNA was essentially eliminated (Figure 4B), indicating efficient nonsense-mediated decay (NMD).
evidence: This is shown by qRT-PCR data in Figure 4B.

claim: Double TALEN Ki-67 knockout cell lines had no residual Ki-67 protein expression.
source: These cell lines had no residual Ki-67 protein expression (Figure 4C), confirming that the basal immunostaining seen in clones 14 and 21 indeed reflected trace level Ki-67 expression.
evidence: This is shown by Western blot and immunofluorescence in Figure 4C.

claim: Ki-67-negative cells proliferated normally.
source: These Ki-67-negative cells proliferated normally.
evidence: This is shown by growth curves and cell cycle analysis in Figure 4D.

claim: Growth curves and DNA content profiles were indistinguishable between WT and Ki-67 null clones.
source: Growth curves and DNA content profiles were indistinguishable from controls (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Cell division time was not significantly different between WT and Ki-67 null clones as determined by time-lapse videomicroscopy.
source: Time-lapse videomicroscopy showed that although individual clones had slightly different cell cycle lengths, cell division time was not significantly different between WT and mutant clones (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Mitotic cells of one Ki-67 null clone had an altered chromosomal periphery.
source: We noticed that mitotic cells of one of the clones lacking Ki-67 had an altered chromosomal periphery (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence in Figure 4F.

claim: An altered chromosomal periphery phenotype has previously been reported in Ki-67 knockdown HeLa cells.
source: Such a phenotype has previously been reported in Ki-67 knockdown HeLa cells (Booth et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 null cells with altered chromosomal periphery could divide efficiently.
source: Nevertheless, these cells could divide efficiently.
evidence: This is an observation from the cell culture experiments.

claim: 42% of WT Mki67 cells could still incorporate some level of EdU even after 72 hr with 0.1% serum.
source: We found that 42% of WT Mki67 cells could still incorporate some level of EdU even after 72 hr with 0.1% serum, but only 13% or 28% of mutant clones 60 or 65, respectively, could do so (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry data in Figure 5A.

claim: Only 13% of mutant clone 60 cells could incorporate EdU after 72 hr with 0.1% serum.
source: We found that 42% of WT Mki67 cells could still incorporate some level of EdU even after 72 hr with 0.1% serum, but only 13% or 28% of mutant clones 60 or 65, respectively, could do so (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Only 28% of mutant clone 65 cells could incorporate EdU after 72 hr with 0.1% serum.
source: We found that 42% of WT Mki67 cells could still incorporate some level of EdU even after 72 hr with 0.1% serum, but only 13% or 28% of mutant clones 60 or 65, respectively, could do so (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Mki67 disruption rendered cells slightly more sensitive to serum starvation.
source: This suggested that Mki67 disruption rendered cells slightly more sensitive to serum starvation.
evidence: This is an inference from the EdU incorporation data after serum starvation.

claim: Upon addition of serum to quiescent cells, WT and Mki67 mutants entered the cell cycle with similar kinetics.
source: Upon addition of serum to quiescent cells, WT and Mki67 mutants entered the cell cycle with similar kinetics (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry data in Figure 5A.

claim: Ki-67 remained completely undetectable in mutants during cell cycle re-entry.
source: Ki-67 remained completely undetectable in mutants (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is shown by Western blot in Figure 5B.

claim: Inducing shRNA expression in BJ-hTERT cells largely prevented Ki-67 expression but had no detectable effect on the kinetics of entry into the cell cycle.
source: In BJ-hTERT, inducing shRNA expression largely prevented Ki-67 expression but had no detectable effect on the kinetics of entry into the cell cycle, as judged by expression of cell cycle regulators and EdU incorporation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Further reducing residual Ki-67 levels with siRNA in BJ-hTERT cells did not affect cell proliferation.
source: Further reducing residual Ki-67 levels with siRNA also did not affect cell proliferation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Constitutive knockdown of Ki-67 in stable shRNA-expressing HeLa or U2OS cells had no effect on cell cycle distribution.
source: Similarly, constitutive knockdown of Ki-67 in stable shRNA-expressing HeLa or U2OS cells had no effect on cell cycle distribution nor on the expression of cell cycle regulators (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Constitutive knockdown of Ki-67 in stable shRNA-expressing HeLa or U2OS cells had no effect on the expression of cell cycle regulators.
source: Similarly, constitutive knockdown of Ki-67 in stable shRNA-expressing HeLa or U2OS cells had no effect on cell cycle distribution nor on the expression of cell cycle regulators (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: U2OS knockdown cells with undetectable Ki-67 expression incorporated EdU in a similar manner to control cells.
source: Analysing single cells by immunofluorescence showed that knockdown U2OS cells with undetectable Ki-67 expression incorporated EdU in a similar manner to control cells, demonstrating efficient DNA synthesis (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Mammalian cells can proliferate efficiently in the absence of detectable Ki-67.
source: Taken together, these results show that although Ki-67 elimination might have minor effects on cell cycle exit and mitosis, mammalian cells can nevertheless proliferate efficiently in the absence of detectable Ki-67.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the collective experimental data on Ki-67 knockout and knockdown cells.

claim: Ki-67 elimination might have minor effects on cell cycle exit.
source: Taken together, these results show that although Ki-67 elimination might have minor effects on cell cycle exit and mitosis, mammalian cells can nevertheless proliferate efficiently in the absence of detectable Ki-67.
evidence: This is inferred from the serum starvation experiments.

claim: Ki-67 elimination might have minor effects on mitosis.
source: Taken together, these results show that although Ki-67 elimination might have minor effects on cell cycle exit and mitosis, mammalian cells can nevertheless proliferate efficiently in the absence of detectable Ki-67.
evidence: This is inferred from the altered chromosomal periphery phenotype.

claim: Mass spectrometry identified 406 proteins specific to the Ki-67 pulldown.
source: This approach identified 406 proteins specific to the Ki-67 pulldown (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Known Ki-67 partners identified included CDK1, an established Ki-67 kinase.
source: These included known Ki-67 partners: CDK1, an established Ki-67 kinase (Blethrow et al., 2008), nucleolar protein NIFK (Takagi et al., 2001), protein phosphatase 1 (Booth et al., 2014), and five subunits (HCFC1, HSPA8, MATRIN3, RBBP5 and WDR5) of a histone methylase complex that interacts with the nuclear receptor coregulator NRC (also known as NCOA6; Garapaty et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Known Ki-67 partners identified included nucleolar protein NIFK.
source: These included known Ki-67 partners: CDK1, an established Ki-67 kinase (Blethrow et al., 2008), nucleolar protein NIFK (Takagi et al., 2001), protein phosphatase 1 (Booth et al., 2014), and five subunits (HCFC1, HSPA8, MATRIN3, RBBP5 and WDR5) of a histone methylase complex that interacts with the nuclear receptor coregulator NRC (also known as NCOA6; Garapaty et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Known Ki-67 partners identified included protein phosphatase 1.
source: These included known Ki-67 partners: CDK1, an established Ki-67 kinase (Blethrow et al., 2008), nucleolar protein NIFK (Takagi et al., 2001), protein phosphatase 1 (Booth et al., 2014), and five subunits (HCFC1, HSPA8, MATRIN3, RBBP5 and WDR5) of a histone methylase complex that interacts with the nuclear receptor coregulator NRC (also known as NCOA6; Garapaty et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Known Ki-67 partners identified included five subunits (HCFC1, HSPA8, MATRIN3, RBBP5 and WDR5) of a histone methylase complex that interacts with NRC.
source: These included known Ki-67 partners: CDK1, an established Ki-67 kinase (Blethrow et al., 2008), nucleolar protein NIFK (Takagi et al., 2001), protein phosphatase 1 (Booth et al., 2014), and five subunits (HCFC1, HSPA8, MATRIN3, RBBP5 and WDR5) of a histone methylase complex that interacts with the nuclear receptor coregulator NRC (also known as NCOA6; Garapaty et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Gene ontology and STRING analysis classified the Ki-67 interactors as being enriched in chromatin regulation and ribosomal biogenesis.
source: Gene ontology and STRING analysis classified the Ki-67 interactors as being enriched in two general processes: chromatin regulation and ribosomal biogenesis (Figure 6, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ki-67 interactors could be subdivided into groups involved in chromatin modification and transcription, ribosomal subunit biogenesis, pre-rRNA processing, protein translation, and splicing.
source: Specifically, interactors could be subdivided into groups involved in chromatin modification and transcription, ribosomal subunit biogenesis, pre-rRNA processing, protein translation, and splicing.
evidence: This is based on functional classification of the interactors identified by mass spectrometry.

claim: Among chromatin regulators interacting with Ki-67, the NRC-interacting methylase complex was found.
source: Among chromatin regulators interacting with Ki-67, we found the NRC-interacting methylase complex; KMT2D, ASH2L and SUZ12 proteins which are components of MLL and PRC2/EED-EZH1 complexes which regulate histone H3 methylation (Patel et al., 2009; Pasini et al., 2004); SETD1A, HCFC1, HDAC2, YY1 and RCOR1, which are components of H3K4 demethylase complexes and co-repressors; and UHRF1, which binds to H3K9me3-modified chromatin and is involved in both maintaining DNA methylation and heterochromatin formation (Bostick et al., 2007; Guetg et al., 2010; Rottach et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data and citations.

claim: KMT2D, ASH2L and SUZ12 proteins are components of MLL and PRC2/EED-EZH1 complexes which regulate histone H3 methylation.
source: Among chromatin regulators interacting with Ki-67, we found the NRC-interacting methylase complex; KMT2D, ASH2L and SUZ12 proteins which are components of MLL and PRC2/EED-EZH1 complexes which regulate histone H3 methylation (Patel et al., 2009; Pasini et al., 2004); SETD1A, HCFC1, HDAC2, YY1 and RCOR1, which are components of H3K4 demethylase complexes and co-repressors; and UHRF1, which binds to H3K9me3-modified chromatin and is involved in both maintaining DNA methylation and heterochromatin formation (Bostick et al., 2007; Guetg et al., 2010; Rottach et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: SETD1A, HCFC1, HDAC2, YY1 and RCOR1 are components of H3K4 demethylase complexes and co-repressors.
source: Among chromatin regulators interacting with Ki-67, we found the NRC-interacting methylase complex; KMT2D, ASH2L and SUZ12 proteins which are components of MLL and PRC2/EED-EZH1 complexes which regulate histone H3 methylation (Patel et al., 2009; Pasini et al., 2004); SETD1A, HCFC1, HDAC2, YY1 and RCOR1, which are components of H3K4 demethylase complexes and co-repressors; and UHRF1, which binds to H3K9me3-modified chromatin and is involved in both maintaining DNA methylation and heterochromatin formation (Bostick et al., 2007; Guetg et al., 2010; Rottach et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on known functions of these proteins.

claim: UHRF1 binds to H3K9me3-modified chromatin and is involved in both maintaining DNA methylation and heterochromatin formation.
source: Among chromatin regulators interacting with Ki-67, we found the NRC-interacting methylase complex; KMT2D, ASH2L and SUZ12 proteins which are components of MLL and PRC2/EED-EZH1 complexes which regulate histone H3 methylation (Patel et al., 2009; Pasini et al., 2004); SETD1A, HCFC1, HDAC2, YY1 and RCOR1, which are components of H3K4 demethylase complexes and co-repressors; and UHRF1, which binds to H3K9me3-modified chromatin and is involved in both maintaining DNA methylation and heterochromatin formation (Bostick et al., 2007; Guetg et al., 2010; Rottach et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 interacts with TIP5, the major component of the nucleolar remodelling complex (NoRC).
source: Ki-67 also interacts with TIP5, the major component of the nucleolar remodelling complex (NoRC) which is required to establish and maintain perinucleolar heterochromatic rDNA, as well as NoRC-interacting proteins TTF1 and DNM3.
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry data.

claim: NoRC is required to establish and maintain perinucleolar heterochromatic rDNA.
source: Ki-67 also interacts with TIP5, the major component of the nucleolar remodelling complex (NoRC) which is required to establish and maintain perinucleolar heterochromatic rDNA, as well as NoRC-interacting proteins TTF1 and DNM3.
evidence: This is established knowledge about NoRC function.

claim: Ki-67 interacts with NoRC-interacting proteins TTF1 and DNM3.
source: Ki-67 also interacts with TIP5, the major component of the nucleolar remodelling complex (NoRC) which is required to establish and maintain perinucleolar heterochromatic rDNA, as well as NoRC-interacting proteins TTF1 and DNM3.
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry data.

claim: One of the candidate Ki-67 interactors involved in rRNA biogenesis was the Pescadillo homologue PES1.
source: One of the candidate Ki-67 interactors involved in rRNA biogenesis was the Pescadillo homologue PES1, which participates in pre-rRNA processing and is localised in the nucleolar granular components (GC) (Rohrmoser et al., 2007; Tafforeau et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry data and citations.

claim: PES1 participates in pre-rRNA processing and is localised in the nucleolar granular components.
source: One of the candidate Ki-67 interactors involved in rRNA biogenesis was the Pescadillo homologue PES1, which participates in pre-rRNA processing and is localised in the nucleolar granular components (GC) (Rohrmoser et al., 2007; Tafforeau et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: During interphase, Ki-67 localised at the cortical periphery of the GC.
source: During interphase, we found that Ki-67 localised at the cortical periphery of the GC, visualised using PES1.
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence in Figure 7A.

claim: Ki-67 formed a boundary between the perinucleolar heterochromatin and the GC.
source: Ki-67 formed a boundary between the perinucleolar heterochromatin (clearly visible as a 'ring' in the DAPI staining) and the GC (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nucleolar disruption using Actinomycin D caused nuclear relocalisation of Ki-67 and GC proteins.
source: Whereas nucleolar disruption using Actinomycin D or the CDK inhibitors DRB or Roscovitine caused nuclear relocalisation of Ki-67 and GC proteins (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), depletion of Ki-67 did not affect the gross structure of the nucleolus, as determined by PES1 staining (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Nucleolar disruption using CDK inhibitors DRB or Roscovitine caused nuclear relocalisation of Ki-67 and GC proteins.
source: Whereas nucleolar disruption using Actinomycin D or the CDK inhibitors DRB or Roscovitine caused nuclear relocalisation of Ki-67 and GC proteins (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), depletion of Ki-67 did not affect the gross structure of the nucleolus, as determined by PES1 staining (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Depletion of Ki-67 did not affect the gross structure of the nucleolus, as determined by PES1 staining.
source: Whereas nucleolar disruption using Actinomycin D or the CDK inhibitors DRB or Roscovitine caused nuclear relocalisation of Ki-67 and GC proteins (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), depletion of Ki-67 did not affect the gross structure of the nucleolus, as determined by PES1 staining (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 3.

claim: Ki-67 depletion totally disrupted PR formation.
source: Remarkably, we found that Ki-67 depletion totally disrupted PR formation and PES1 no longer associated with the chromosome surface (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Upon Ki-67 depletion, PES1 no longer associated with the chromosome surface.
source: Remarkably, we found that Ki-67 depletion totally disrupted PR formation and PES1 no longer associated with the chromosome surface (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7B.

claim: A similar finding of disrupted PR formation upon Ki-67 depletion, using other nucleolar proteins as PR markers, was recently reported.
source: A similar finding, using other nucleolar proteins than PES1 as PR markers, was recently reported (Booth et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Ki-67 knocked down U2OS cells could still incorporate normal levels of 5-ethynyl uridine (EU) in nucleolar RNA.
source: We found that Ki-67 knocked down U2OS cells, that have essentially undetectable Ki-67, could still incorporate normal levels of 5-ethynyl uridine (EU) in nucleolar RNA.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: rRNA transcription is not altered in Ki-67 knockdown cells.
source: This suggests that rRNA transcription is not altered (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the EU incorporation data in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Silencing Ki-67 expression by shRNA or siRNA had no significant effect on pre-rRNA processing in four different cancer cell lines.
source: This showed that silencing Ki-67 expression by shRNA or siRNA had no significant effect on pre-rRNA processing in four different cancer cell lines (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is shown by Northern blot analysis in Figure 8A.

claim: A marginal but reproducible increase in the level of the 47S precursor rRNA was observed upon Ki-67 depletion, indicating a mild delay in the early nucleolar pre-rRNA cleavage steps.
source: We did, however, notice a marginal but reproducible increase in the level of the 47S precursor rRNA, indicating a mild delay in the early nucleolar pre-rRNA cleavage steps (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Impairment of early pre-rRNA cleavage steps upon depletion of Ki-67 was independent of p53.
source: Impairment of early pre-rRNA cleavage steps upon depletion of Ki-67 was independent of p53 (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is shown by experiments in p53-null cells in Figure 8B.

claim: Ki-67 is dispensable for efficient pre-rRNA processing.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that while Ki-67 is dispensable for efficient pre-rRNA processing, it is essential for the formation of the perichromosomal layer during nucleologenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pre-rRNA processing data.

claim: Ki-67 is essential for the formation of the perichromosomal layer during nucleologenesis.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that while Ki-67 is dispensable for efficient pre-rRNA processing, it is essential for the formation of the perichromosomal layer during nucleologenesis.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the PR formation experiments in Figure 7B.

claim: Ki-67 knockdown led to downregulation of over 200 genes (corrected p value <0.02, Fold-change >1.5).
source: Ki-67 knockdown led to downregulation (corrected p value <0.02, Fold-change >1.5) of over 200 genes (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is shown by microarray analysis in Figure 8C.

claim: Expression of cell cycle regulatory genes was not affected by Ki-67 knockdown.
source: Expression of cell cycle regulatory genes was not affected.
evidence: This is based on the transcriptome analysis.

claim: Ki-67 silencing caused upregulation of a wide variety of genes involved in neural, testis and cardiovascular system development and differentiation.
source: Additionally, Ki-67 silencing caused upregulation (corrected p value <0.02, Fold-change >1.5) of a wide variety of genes involved in neural, testis and cardiovascular system development and differentiation (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is shown by microarray analysis in Figure 8C.

claim: Upregulated genes upon Ki-67 silencing were strikingly enriched in genes encoding zinc-finger proteins and olfactory receptors.
source: These were strikingly enriched in genes encoding zinc-finger proteins and olfactory receptors, two gene families that are highly enriched in nucleolar associated-domains (NADs) of perinucleolar heterochromatin (PNHC) (Németh et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on gene ontology analysis of the transcriptome data and supported by a citation.

claim: Zinc-finger proteins and olfactory receptors are two gene families that are highly enriched in nucleolar associated-domains (NADs) of perinucleolar heterochromatin.
source: These were strikingly enriched in genes encoding zinc-finger proteins and olfactory receptors, two gene families that are highly enriched in nucleolar associated-domains (NADs) of perinucleolar heterochromatin (PNHC) (Németh et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Effects of Ki-67 downregulation on gene expression might be due to an altered chromatin state, in particular of PNHC.
source: This suggested that effects of Ki-67 downregulation on gene expression might be due to an altered chromatin state, in particular of PNHC.
evidence: This is an inference from the gene expression data.

claim: Ki-67 knockdown in HeLa and U2OS cells caused a marked reduction in perinucleolar DAPI staining.
source: In support of a potential role for Ki-67 in heterochromatin organisation, we found that Ki-67 knockdown in HeLa and U2OS cells caused a marked reduction in perinucleolar DAPI staining (Figure 7A, 9A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7A and Figure 9A.

claim: Upon Ki-67 depletion, the mean FRET percentage decreased, reflecting a reduction in total chromatin compaction.
source: Upon Ki-67 depletion, the mean FRET percentage decreased, reflecting a reduction in total chromatin compaction (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is shown by FRET-FLIM analysis in Figure 9B.

claim: The highest FRET populations, including heterochromatin regions at the nuclear periphery and around nucleoli, were largely eliminated upon Ki-67 depletion.
source: The highest FRET populations, including heterochromatin regions at the nuclear periphery and around nucleoli, were largely eliminated upon Ki-67 depletion, with a few remaining condensed foci predominantly located at the nuclear periphery (Figure 9C,D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 9C and 9D.

claim: A population of less compact chromatin increased upon Ki-67 depletion.
source: In contrast, a population of less compact chromatin increased.
evidence: This is shown by FRET-FLIM analysis in Figure 9C and 9D.

claim: In HeLa and U2OS cells, CENP-A showed a non-random nuclear localisation and clustered around nucleoli.
source: In HeLa and U2OS cells, CENP-A showed a non-random nuclear localisation and clustered around nucleoli (Figure 9E, arrowheads), confirming that CENP-A can be used as a surrogate marker for adjacent pericentromeric DNA.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 9E.

claim: CENP-A can be used as a surrogate marker for adjacent pericentromeric DNA.
source: In HeLa and U2OS cells, CENP-A showed a non-random nuclear localisation and clustered around nucleoli (Figure 9E, arrowheads), confirming that CENP-A can be used as a surrogate marker for adjacent pericentromeric DNA.
evidence: This is inferred from the CENP-A localization pattern.

claim: Upon Ki-67 knockdown, the interaction between perinucleolar and pericentromeric heterochromatin was disrupted, and the CENP-A signal was dispersed throughout the nucleus.
source: Consistent with our hypothesis, this interaction was disrupted upon Ki-67 knockdown, and the CENP-A signal was no longer grouped around nucleoli but dispersed throughout the nucleus (Figure 9E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 9E.

claim: Ki-67 mediates interaction between different regions in the genome that are normally packaged into heterochromatin.
source: These results imply that Ki-67 mediates interaction between different regions in the genome that are normally packaged into heterochromatin, and could potentially maintain silencing of genes by recruiting them to constitutive heterochromatin.
evidence: This is inferred from the CENP-A localization and FRET data.

claim: Ki-67 could potentially maintain silencing of genes by recruiting them to constitutive heterochromatin.
source: These results imply that Ki-67 mediates interaction between different regions in the genome that are normally packaged into heterochromatin, and could potentially maintain silencing of genes by recruiting them to constitutive heterochromatin.
evidence: This is a speculative inference from the data.

claim: Stable shRNA-mediated Ki-67 knockdown in HeLa, U2OS and inducible knockdown in BJ-hTERT fibroblasts caused a visible reduction in nucleolar staining of H3K9me3 and H4K20me3.
source: Stable shRNA-mediated Ki-67 knockdown in HeLa, U2OS and inducible knockdown in BJ-hTERT fibroblasts caused a visible reduction in nucleolar staining of H3K9me3 and H4K20me3 (Figure 10—figure supplements 1–3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 10—figure supplements 1-3.

claim: Upon Ki-67 knockdown, H3K9me3 and H4K20me3 marks were relocalised either to foci in proximity to the nucleolus or a punctate pattern dispersed throughout the nucleus.
source: This mark was relocalised either to foci in proximity to the nucleolus or a punctate pattern dispersed throughout the nucleus.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 10—figure supplements 1-3.

claim: In mouse cells, H3K9me3 staining colocalised with DAPI-dense chromocentres.
source: In mouse cells, where pericentromeric heterochromatin is prominent, H3K9me3 staining colocalised with DAPI-dense chromocentres, but TALEN-ablation of Mki67 resulted in general nuclear punctate H3K9me3 that was excluded from nucleoli (Figure 10A,B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 10A and 10B.

claim: TALEN-ablation of Mki67 in mouse cells resulted in general nuclear punctate H3K9me3 that was excluded from nucleoli.
source: In mouse cells, where pericentromeric heterochromatin is prominent, H3K9me3 staining colocalised with DAPI-dense chromocentres, but TALEN-ablation of Mki67 resulted in general nuclear punctate H3K9me3 that was excluded from nucleoli (Figure 10A,B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 10A and 10B.

claim: Ki-67 depletion did not affect the overall levels of H3K9me3 and H4K20me3 chromatin modifications.
source: Western blotting revealed that Ki-67 depletion did not affect the overall levels of these chromatin modifications (Figure 10—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 4.

claim: Despite the loss of intense H3K9me3 staining regions in Mki67 mutant cells, all three HP1 isoforms maintained their localisation at DAPI-dense regions.
source: Immunofluoresence showed that, surprisingly, despite the loss of the intense H3K9me3 staining regions in the Mki67 mutant cells, all three HP1 isoforms maintained their localisation at DAPI-dense regions (Figure 10—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 5.

claim: In control cells, major satellite DNA, DAPI-dense regions and H3K9me3 largely colocalised.
source: In control cells, major satellite DNA, DAPI-dense regions and H3K9me3 largely colocalised (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is shown by combined immunofluorescence and FISH in Figure 10C.

claim: In cells lacking Ki-67, major satellite DNA was still present at regions of compacted DNA, despite the loss of H3K9me3 at these regions.
source: In cells lacking Ki-67, major satellite DNA was still present at regions of compacted DNA, despite the loss of H3K9me3 at these regions (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 10C.

claim: Ki-67 is required for maintaining heterochromatic histone marks at genomic regions that are organised into heterochromatin.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that Ki-67 is required for maintaining heterochromatic histone marks at genomic regions that are organised into heterochromatin.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the histone modification localization data.

claim: There was a strong correlation between cells with higher levels of exogenous Ki-67 and appearance of DAPI-dense foci resembling ectopic heterochromatin, marked by H3K9me3 and HP1.
source: There was a strong correlation between cells with higher levels of exogenous Ki-67 and appearance of DAPI-dense foci resembling ectopic heterochromatin, marked by H3K9me3 and HP1 (Figure 11A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 11A.

claim: Cells showing ectopic heterochromatin due to Ki-67 overexpression were negative for cyclin A staining, suggesting that they were unable to enter S-phase.
source: Cells showing this phenotype were negative for cyclin A staining, suggesting that they were unable to enter S-phase, whereas lower expression did not prevent cyclin A accumulation (Figure 11B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 11B and is an inference from the cyclin A staining.

claim: Cells with ectopic heterochromatin due to Ki-67 overexpression were negative for histone H3 Ser-10 phosphorylation, a mitotic marker.
source: They were also negative for histone H3 Ser-10 phosphorylation, a mitotic marker (Figure 11—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 11—figure supplement 1.

claim: A putative Xenopus Ki-67 homologue was identified in a proteomics-based screen for proteins associated with replicating chromatin in egg extracts.
source: In a proteomics-based screen for proteins associated with replicating chromatin in egg extracts, we identified a putative Xenopus Ki-67 homologue (Figure 11—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 11—figure supplement 2.

claim: In interphase, exogenous Xenopus Ki-67 is present ubiquitously on chromatin.
source: Whereas in interphase, exogenous Xenopus Ki-67 is present ubiquitously on chromatin, it colocalises with endogenous Ki-67 in mitosis at the perichromosomal region (Figure 11C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 11C.

claim: Exogenous Xenopus Ki-67 colocalises with endogenous Ki-67 in mitosis at the perichromosomal region.
source: Whereas in interphase, exogenous Xenopus Ki-67 is present ubiquitously on chromatin, it colocalises with endogenous Ki-67 in mitosis at the perichromosomal region (Figure 11C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 11C.

claim: Overexpression of Xenopus Ki-67 caused extreme chromatin compaction.
source: Overexpression of Xenopus Ki-67, like human Ki-67, caused extreme chromatin compaction (Figure 11C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 11C.

claim: Controlling heterochromatin is a conserved essential function of Ki-67.
source: We conclude that controlling heterochromatin is a conserved essential function of Ki-67.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the functional conservation between human and Xenopus Ki-67.
